newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down, profit-taking, weak economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down, profit-taking, weak economy.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 2.05 percent lower on Thursday as investors sold communication and energy issues to take profits and shrugged off leading monthly indicators released by the central bank, brokers said.
"Even key foreign reserves figures which did not look so bad failed to help the market. Investors are still worried about the country's economy," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The composite SET index closed 13.91 points lower at 665.62 on on 5.2 billion baht turnover.
The Bank of Thailand said earlier on Thursday that foreign reserves fell to $32.4 billion in June from $33.3 billion in May. This figure was above market expectations.
"But investors decided to sell as they think that impact on the economy would probably be seen in the figure for July when the country floated its currency," said Thanawat.
The baht, previously pegged against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar, has depreciated around 20 percent since it was floated on July 2.
The property sector was the only major sector that gained on Thursday, rising 0.52 percent.

The finance sector was the most active counter in terms of value, losing 1.12 percent, followed by the banking counter, which shed 1.46 percent, and the communication sector, which retreated 4.94 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 116. TelecomAsia slipped 4.75 to 44 and Securities One lost 4.25 to 45.25.
